_about: Dynamic package gate rules. package-gate.ps1 evaluates every rule here against a package folder (and, when given, its Nexus distro folder and the previous release) and exits non-zero on any hit. ADD A ROW WHEN A CLASS OF DEFECT SHIPS OR NEARLY SHIPS - the same day, beside the logic-library entry. The owner, 2026-09-16: 'come up with a way to dynamically add logic gates to close logic loops as needed when possible instead of just adding to the logic library'. Kinds: see package-gate.ps1's header - forbid-path-regex, forbid-extension, esp-must-be-light, no-doubled-segment, keep-file-classes-of-previous, archive-matches-folder, page-text-forbid-regex, page-text-require-regex, require-file-content-regex, changelog-top-version, distro-file-first-line, translations-complete, lines-match-build-tree, dll-newer-than-sources, page-summary-max-chars, forbid-file-content-regex, esp-record-integrity, json-parses, swf-colour-band, distro-images-are-sdr, launch-gate (a launch gate's row: the package gate only checks it is still wired into its launcher). 'exemptMods' matches the mod's display name or ledger key. 'kinds' limits a rule to the registry kinds listed (skse-mod, or-mod, w3-mod, mo2-plugin, mo2-theme, skyrim-asset, tool).

Logic library 46 (routing a page's literals through a string table: three ways the tooling passes while strings stay English) and the eleven-languages rule: a language file that lacks a key english has falls back to English silently.

Logic library 5364 (a mod with two build lines will happily package the WRONG one, and only the strictest mod complains) and section 13 of the 2026-09-16 handoff: package-mod.ps1 picks 'the newest DLL with a PDB' and shipped the 1.7 DLL where SE was needed. If the repo has both build trees, the package ships both, each byte-identical to its tree and stamped with the version.

Logic library 2068 (a failed build followed by package-mod.ps1 ships the PREVIOUS DLL under the NEW version number), 1857 (build AFTER the version bump) and 2135 (stamp the version BEFORE the build that a gate uses). A packaged DLL older than any source file or CMakeLists.txt was not built from what the repo says it was.
rules.amended: 2026-10-25 (Apocrypha Menu Framework 2.3.0): each DLL is compared with ITS OWN sources when the repo maps them in tools\dll-sources.json ({"dlls": [{"dll": "<file name>", "sources": "<regex over the repo-relative path, / separators>"}]}); a DLL the map does not name, and every DLL of a repo without a map, is still compared with every source. Ysgramor's Armor addon 1.0.0 reached the test install with form version 0 in its TES4 header and in every record its builder wrote - MO2 flagged it as a form-0 (pre-SE) plugin. The header of a plugin we ship is Skyrim SE's 44. Records are NOT required to be 44: a record copied from a master keeps the master's form version, and stamping 44 onto a record that carries a 12-byte BODT made the engine read it as an 8-byte BOD2 and crash before the menu (Nordic Dragonbone 1.0.1, 2026-09-16). No real record is form 0, so any form-0 record is a hand-written header and fails.

rules.fix: call AddressLibraryGuard::Guard(<mod name>) BEFORE SKSE::Init(a_skse): CommonLibSSE-NG's Init opens the Address Library itself (REL::IDDatabase::get()), so a guard placed after it never runs when the file is missing

A guard that runs after the thing it guards is not a guard.

rules.fix: call AddressLibraryGuard::Guard(<mod name>) once, before SKSE::Init, and read AddressLibraryGuard::Last() if the report is wanted again after the mod's logger exists - never call Check() from a mod's own source
rules.why: Apocrypha Menu Framework 1.9.3 called Check() a second time after SKSE::Init so its logger could carry the Address Library line. The game then died about a second after launch, before SKSE wrote a line of its own log and with no message box, and every profile that build won in was unbootable (the owner, 2026-09-18: '1.9.2 boots but not 1.9.3'). The guard is a pre-flight that runs once; the report it made is kept in Last() for anyone who needs it later.

Civil War Guard Armor Replacer shipped a Tullius container whose COCT still said five after two CNTO entries were removed. The engine trusts the count and read past the list, so the game crashed at data load inside SPID and the crash log named SPID, not us. The plugin parsed and opened cleanly in xEdit; only counting the entries catches it. The same check covers LLCT/LVLO on levelled lists, KSIZ/KWDA, one MODL per armature addon, and a reference to a record the file does not define.

No DATA reads as flags 0, so the CS Water patch built on it wrote the cell as exterior, and the game crashed on a null worldspace (2026-11-05). rules.fix: rebuild the plugin with merge-to-espfe.py (it now writes the group tree through esp_groups.py), or repair the file as it stands with esp-regroup.py <plugin> --out <fixed> --parents-from <the source mod or master that places each record> [--assign FID-FID=CELL] - it moves REFR/INFO into their CELL/DIAL children groups and proves every other record byte-identical
rules.why: Civil War Guard Armor Replacer 1.0.0's merged plugin carried top-level REFR and INFO groups and loose CELL records in its CELL group, because merge-to-espfe.py flattened its sources' group trees. A Mutagen patcher refused the file ('Read in data that was not a GRUP'), so any Synthesis patcher reading every group fails on it, and Mutagen's full import silently dropped every cell, reference and dialogue response (1238 of 1312 records). esp-audit.py checks the whole tree (no top-level child-type group, CELL block > sub-block > CELL + children > placed records, DIAL + topic children > INFO, a plain top group holds only its own type); 1996 Njordlinger plugins plus Skyrim.esm and Update.esm pass it and only this plugin failed. Regression test: scripts/tests/test_esp_group_tree.py. plugin-gate.ps1 now audits 'unpublished *' mod folders too: the plugin had been enabled through every launch while esp-audit's top-level-label check (added 2026-09-21) failed it, because the launch gate only looked at 'test *' folders.

rules.fix: the record's model hashes came from a record below form 40: drop MODT/MO2T-MO5T/DMDT from it (they are optional) or carry the source record's own form version through; never stamp 44 over them
rules.why: Campfire Camp Addon 1.0.0 crashed the game while loading its plugin. Its build script copied MODT from Skyrim.esm's form-39 StockadeScaffoldTop0Sided01Planks into a form-44 STAT. Below form 40 MODT is flat 12-byte triples; from form 40 it starts with a header, and Skyrim 1.5.97's parser ([id removed], called by the STAT loader, [id removed]) read the first hash as the header count and went to a wild address. The plugin parsed and passed esp-audit, because nothing compared MODT's size with its own header. Every record at form 40 or later must now satisfy size == 4 + 4*H + 12*textures + 4*addons, which all 14727 such subrecords in Skyrim.esm and Update.esm and all 118582 in 2040 third-party plugins do.

A Dynamic Interface Patcher descriptor written from PowerShell kept a single backslash in a Data-relative path, so the patcher reported invalid_escape and applied nothing - a patch that ships and does nothing looks exactly like a patch that was never made. Any .json we ship (DIP descriptors, SPID-adjacent configs, settings presets) must parse.

rules.fix: a Scaleform / GFx call (GFxValue Invoke/SetMember/GetMember, GFxMovie Invoke/SetVariable/GetVariable, loadClip, getBounds, anything on uiMovie) never runs inside an SKSE AddTask lambda: queue it with SKSE::GetTaskInterface()->AddUITask(...) (runs inside the UI's own message processing, the thread the movies advance on), or raise a flag the menu serves from its own AdvanceMovie / ProcessMessage. Reference: Dragon's Eye Minimap commit c23a199 (1.7.6) - RequestDisplayApply() only raises a flag, Minimap::Advance() applies it on the HUD thread at most once per 120 ms, and OnMainThread / the DevBench tasks use AddUITask.

rules.note: Reads the BODY of each AddTask lambda only (.NET balancing groups track its braces; comments, string and raw-string literals are skipped, so a brace or a token inside them does not count), and only direct calls written there. AddUITask lambdas are not matched. A call one step away - the lambda calls a helper of the mod's that makes the calls, or the lambda goes through a wrapper that forwards to AddTask, as DEM 1.7.5's did - is row scaleform-helpers-only-on-the-ui-thread's business. Regression test: scripts/tests/test_gate_scaleform_calls_only_on_the_ui_thread.py (covers both rows).

rules.fix: the helper an AddTask lambda calls (or the wrapper that forwards a lambda to AddTask) makes Scaleform calls: queue that work with AddUITask instead, or raise a flag the menu serves from its own AdvanceMovie / ProcessMessage. Reference: Dragon's Eye Minimap commit c23a199 (1.7.6) - RequestDisplayApply + Minimap::Advance(), and OnMainThread switched to AddUITask.
rules.why: Dragon's Eye Minimap 1.7.5's crashing calls were one step away from the AddTask lambda: the settings page handed []{ minimap->ApplyDisplaySettings(); } to OnMainThread, which forwarded it to AddTask, and ApplyDisplaySettings made the SetMember / getBounds calls - so the direct regex row (scaleform-calls-only-on-the-ui-thread) would have passed it. This script refuses that shape: an AddTask lambda or AddTask(Function) reaching a same-repo function whose body makes Scaleform calls, or a lambda handed to a wrapper that forwards to AddTask making them itself or through such a function. rules.note: One call deep. A helper counts only when every definition of its name in the repo makes Scaleform calls outside an AddUITask lambda and none is an override (Scaleform-called handlers are already on the UI thread); a name shared with an unrelated function is skipped rather than guessed, so it can miss (Compass Navigation Overhaul's compass->SetTextScale shares its name with UI::SetTextScale). rules.fix: resolve the address when it is first needed, inside a function that runs after SKSEPluginLoad's checks: a function-local static (static REL::Relocation<T> f{ id }; inside the hook's install or thunk), a member set in Install() (static inline REL::Relocation<T> f; with no initialiser, assigned there), or an accessor such as Infinity UI's static std::uintptr_t LoadMovieAddress() { return LoadMovieId.address(); }. Keep the ID itself (REL::ID, REL::RelocationID, REL::VariantID) at static scope if wanted - constructing an ID resolves nothing; constructing a Relocation from it, or calling .address() on it, opens the Address Library
rules.why: Infinity UI 2.1.3 (fix 7af23a3, 2026-10-22): Hooks.h held static inline REL::Relocation<...> LoadMovie{ LoadMovieId }. A Relocation built from an Address Library ID resolves its address in its constructor, and a static-member or namespace-scope one is constructed by the C runtime while the DLL loads - before SKSEPluginLoad runs. On Skyrim 1.7.x the SE/AE DLL therefore died with CommonLibSSE-NG's bare 'REL/ID.h(223): failed to open address library file' before the build-line check and the Address Library guard (rows address-library-guard-runs-before-skse-init, skse-plugin-carries-address-library-guard) could run: no guard can run before static initialisation. The pattern walks the file from the top and skips whole function bodies (a ')' then a balanced {...}, comments and string literals honoured), so a function-local static REL::Relocation - resolved on first call - is never flagged; it refuses a REL::Relocation declared with an initialiser outside any function (static inline, namespace scope, class member) unless it is built from REL::Offset / REL::VariantOffset (no Address Library), and a static/inline/const variable outside a function whose initialiser calls .address() on a REL::ID, RelocationID, VariantID or RELOCATION_ID. Sweep of 2026-10-22: Compass Navigation Overhaul, Dragon's Eye Minimap SMF, HUD Position Manager, Inventory Reforged Diag and Local Map Upgrade still carry such statics (24 lines); Infinity UI is clean after 7af23a3.
